msg: security: [] on an operation means "no authentication required". A gateway that imports this spec publishes the endpoint open.
ref: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 - API1 / API5

msg: Top-level security: [] declares the whole API public. Every operation that does not override it is unauthenticated.
This document has paths but no top-level security block. Authentication is then opt-in per operation, so any operation you forget ships open.
An apiKey carried in the query string is written to proxy logs, browser history and Referer headers. Move it to a header.
The OAuth 2.0 implicit grant returns the token in the URL fragment. RFC 9700 (BCP 240, January 2025) says clients MUST NOT use it.
The resource owner password credentials grant hands the user's password to the client. RFC 9700 (BCP 240, January 2025) says it MUST NOT be used.
An OAuth endpoint reached over http:// exposes the authorization code or token to anyone on the path.
A server entry on http:// tells every generated client and gateway to send credentials in the clear.
No server in this document uses https://. There is no transport-secured base URL for a generated client to pick.
HTTP Basic replays a static credential on every call, so it cannot be revoked per session and shows up in memory dumps and logs.
An OAuth flow with no scopes issues one all-or-nothing token, so a read client holds write rights.
A wildcard or catch-all scope defeats the point of scopes: every token that asks for it gets the whole API.
This security scheme is defined but never referenced by any security block, so nothing in the document actually requires it.
This operation documents no 429 response, so generated clients and the gateway have no agreed throttling contract.
additionalProperties: true on a request schema lets a caller post fields you never declared - the classic mass-assignment route.
An operation is marked deprecated but the document names no sunset date, so callers have no removal date to plan against.
ref: RFC 8594 - The Sunset HTTP Header Field

msg: A debug, trace or actuator path is published in the same document you hand to external callers.
This example or default value carries a live-looking credential. Examples are copied into docs, SDKs and test fixtures.
